# TES foundation inventory — the UI stack as it exists

<!-- Generated by tools/tes-ui-stack-inventory.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

## 1. What this is, and what it is not

GE-143-001 asks for an inventory of every current UI stack, component library, CSS strategy,
font, icon set, table/grid, chart library, editor, calendar, dialog, theme, breakpoint and
copied component, and for the duplication, accessibility debt, visual drift and migration risk
that inventory exposes. This document is that inventory, derived from the checkout on the commit
it was generated on.

It is a measurement of SOURCE. It does not open a browser, so it cannot tell you that a control
is hard to hit or that a contrast pair fails in practice — `apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts`
computes the second and §8 names the rest. Both applications with a user interface are scanned;
reading a number here as a statement about only the tenant product would be wrong, which is why
every table is per application.

* **Tenant experience** — `apps/web`, 330 shipping source files scanned.
* **Operator plane** — `apps/system-studio`, 244 shipping source files scanned.

## 2. The concerns the requirement names

**Implementations** are modules that DEFINE the concern; **call sites** are modules that import
one. A page rendering a table is a call site of the table it imports and an implementation only
if it writes its own — which several do, and that is the finding rather than an accident of
counting.

* **UI stack.** The framework and its root document. One per application by construction.
* **Component library.** Owned wrappers over a behaviour library, counted by use: a component three or more modules import. GE-143-002 asks for ONE library, consumed by every surface.
* **CSS strategy.** A global token stylesheet plus utility classes. Every additional strategy is a second place a colour can be decided.
* **Font.** Families are declared in CSS so no build step fetches a remote file. A stylesheet that names a family is a place a font decision lives.
* **Icon set.** One barrel aliasing one family, plus every module that draws its own glyph inline.
* **Table / grid.** GE-143-023 asks for an owned virtualized grid contract. Every module that writes its own <table> is a surface that contract does not cover.
* **Chart library.** Owned SVG marks, no vendor chart engine. GE-143-027 is the decision to select one.
* **Editor.** Structured editing surfaces. A plain `<textarea>` is not one — it is a surface with NO editor module behind it, which is counted separately below because it is the same migration question asked from the other end.
* **Calendar.** Owned grid, recurrence and conflict code rather than a calendar package.
* **Dialog.** GE-143-008 owns the layering; this row is about how many things open one.
* **Theme.** Theme scopes are CSS, resolved before first paint by the root layout's script.
* **Breakpoint.** Widths at which the layout changes. Two stylesheets with different widths is a drift nobody sees until a screenshot.

## 4. Duplication

### 4.1 Concerns implemented separately in both applications

This is the structural duplication GE-143-002 exists to end: there is no shared, versioned TES
package, so each application carries its own answer to the same question. The count is the number
of modules on each side, not a similarity claim — §4.3 is where similarity is measured.

| Concern | Tenant experience | Operator plane |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI stack | 1 | 1 |

| Font | 1 | 15 |

| Editor | 3 | 1 |
| Calendar | 5 | 1 |

### 4.2 Declared and never imported

| App | Package | Declared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `lucide-react` | ^1.24.0 |

A UI dependency nothing imports is the cheapest duplication to remove and the easiest to miss:
it is installed, audited, resolved and shipped in the lockfile, and no surface uses it.

### 4.3 Copied components

Pairs of modules under a `components/` directory whose five-token identifier shingles overlap by
at least 70%. Formatting, comments and copy are stripped first, so
this measures structure rather than prose.

None above the threshold. That is a real result and a narrow one: it says no two components in
one application are near-identical, not that no logic is duplicated. The closest pair in each
application is named so the answer can be checked rather than trusted:

* **Tenant experience** — closest pair 17%: `apps/web/src/components/ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx` and `apps/web/src/components/ui/ConfirmInlineSubmit.tsx`.
* **Operator plane** — closest pair 28%: `apps/system-studio/src/components/md3/Drawer.tsx` and `apps/system-studio/src/components/md3/ModalDialog.tsx`.

## 5. Accessibility debt

Counted from the markup, with the first example of each so the number can be checked rather than
believed. These are shapes, not verdicts: a `div` with an `onClick` MAY be reachable another way.
A signal with a count of zero is stated, because a scan that only prints what it found cannot be
told apart from a scan that found nothing.

| App | Signal | Occurrences | Files | First example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| web | icon-only-control-without-a-name | — | — | — |
| web | image-without-alt-text | — | — | — |
| web | positive-tabindex | — | — | — |
| web | click-handler-on-a-non-interactive-element | 2 | 2 | `<div onClick={closePanel} className={'fixed inset-0 z-assist-scrim bg-black/20 transition-` |
| studio | icon-only-control-without-a-name | — | — | — |
| studio | image-without-alt-text | — | — | — |
| studio | positive-tabindex | — | — | — |
| studio | click-handler-on-a-non-interactive-element | 1 | 1 | `<span data-md3="tree-twisty" aria-hidden="true" onClick={() =>` |

* **icon-only-control-without-a-name** — a control whose whole label is a glyph is announced as 'button' and nothing else.
* **image-without-alt-text** — an image with no alt attribute is either decorative or unreadable, and the markup does not say which.
* **positive-tabindex** — a positive tabindex re-orders the whole document's focus sequence, not just this control's.
* **click-handler-on-a-non-interactive-element** — a div that responds to a mouse does not respond to a keyboard unless it is given a role and a tab stop.

## 6. Visual drift

Values decided outside the token system. Drift is not an aesthetic judgement: it is the measure
of how much of the surface a token change does not reach.

| App | Signal | Occurrences | Files | First example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| web | literal-colour | 37 | 9 | `#198052` |
| web | arbitrary-length-in-a-class | 283 | 66 | `text-[13px]` |
| web | inline-style-object | 97 | 38 | `style={{` |
| studio | literal-colour | — | — | — |
| studio | arbitrary-length-in-a-class | — | — | — |
| studio | inline-style-object | 3 | 3 | `style={{` |

* **literal-colour** — a colour a theme change cannot reach.
* **arbitrary-length-in-a-class** — a size chosen beside the scale rather than from it.
* **inline-style-object** — a declaration no stylesheet, audit or theme can see.

## 7. Migration risk

The band in §2 comes from this rule and nothing else:

* **NONE** — no implementation found.
* **LOW** — one implementation, twenty or fewer call sites.
* **MEDIUM** — one implementation with more than twenty call sites, or up to five implementations.
* **HIGH** — more than five implementations: the concern is spread, so migrating it is a survey first.

The rule is deliberately crude. A band is an ordering of where to look, and a formula nobody can
recompute in their head is a judgement wearing arithmetic's clothes.

## 8. What this inventory does NOT establish

* **That a surface is accessible.** §5 counts markup shapes. Screen-reader behaviour, focus order
  and live-region correctness are not derivable from source and are not claimed.
* **That a token is used correctly.** §6 counts values that bypass the system; it says nothing
  about whether the tokens that ARE used are the right ones.
* **That two applications' components behave alike.** §4.1 counts implementations of a concern on
  each side. Two dialogs are two dialogs whether or not they agree.
* **Anything about a running deployment.** Nothing here opens a browser or reaches a URL.
